$comment: Editorial seed 2026bl: five es/en trivia pairs on brands — famous logos, slogans, food brands, tech brands and car-brand origins — all in pop-culture. Every answer is a stable, checkable fact. The en-car-brands-trivia/es-trivia-marcas-de-autos slugs were already used by batch 2026bi, so the car pair uses the origins angle with distinct slugs. quizzes.title: Brand Logos Trivia: The Stories Behind Famous Symbols
quizzes.description: Eight questions on the secrets of the world's best-known logos, from hidden arrows and bears to a $35 swoosh.

questions.question: The Starbucks logo depicts which mythological figure?
questions.explanation: The Starbucks logo is a twin-tailed siren, chosen in 1971 to evoke the seafaring history of coffee and the port of Seattle.

questions.question: Which delivery company's logo hides a white arrow between the letters 'E' and 'x'?
questions.explanation: The FedEx wordmark, designed in 1994, hides a forward-pointing arrow in the negative space.

questions.question: In Amazon's logo, the arrow under the name runs from the letter 'a' to which letter?
questions.explanation: The smile-shaped arrow runs from A to Z, hinting that the store sells everything.

questions.question: Which carmaker's logo of four interlocking rings stands for the four companies that merged into Auto Union?
questions.explanation: The rings represent Audi, DKW, Horch and Wanderer, the four brands that formed Auto Union in 1932.

questions.question: Which Swiss chocolate bar hides a bear inside the mountain on its logo?
questions.explanation: Toblerone's Matterhorn contains a bear, the symbol of Bern, where the chocolate is made.

questions.question: How much did Nike pay design student Carolyn Davidson for the 'swoosh' logo in 1971?
questions.explanation: Davidson billed $35 for the swoosh; years later Nike gave her company stock and a diamond ring.

questions.question: The blue and white of BMW's roundel come from the flag of which German state?
questions.explanation: The colors echo the Bavarian flag; BMW was founded in Munich in 1916.

questions.question: Which tire company's mascot is Bibendum, a figure made of stacked tires?
questions.explanation: Bibendum, the Michelin Man, has represented the French tire brand since 1898.

quizzes.title: Trivia de logos de marcas: las historias detrás de los símbolos famosos
quizzes.description: Ocho preguntas sobre los secretos de los logos más conocidos del mundo, de flechas y osos escondidos a un swoosh de 35 dólares.

questions.question: ¿Qué figura mitológica muestra el logo de Starbucks?
questions.explanation: El logo de Starbucks es una sirena de dos colas, elegida en 1971 por la historia marinera del café y el puerto de Seattle.

questions.question: ¿Qué empresa de paquetería esconde una flecha blanca entre las letras 'E' y 'x' de su logo?
questions.explanation: El logotipo de FedEx, diseñado en 1994, esconde una flecha que apunta hacia adelante en el espacio negativo.

questions.question: En el logo de Amazon, la flecha bajo el nombre va de la letra 'a' a qué letra?
questions.explanation: La flecha con forma de sonrisa va de la A a la Z, sugiriendo que la tienda vende de todo.

questions.question: ¿Qué fabricante de autos usa cuatro aros entrelazados que representan a las cuatro empresas que formaron Auto Union?
questions.explanation: Los aros representan a Audi, DKW, Horch y Wanderer, las cuatro marcas que formaron Auto Union en 1932.

questions.question: ¿Qué chocolate suizo esconde un oso dentro de la montaña de su logo?
questions.explanation: El Matterhorn de Toblerone esconde un oso, símbolo de Berna, donde se fabrica el chocolate.

questions.question: ¿Cuánto pagó Nike a la estudiante Carolyn Davidson por el logo 'swoosh' en 1971?
questions.explanation: Davidson cobró 35 dólares por el swoosh; años después Nike le regaló acciones y un anillo de diamantes.

questions.question: El azul y el blanco del emblema de BMW vienen de la bandera de qué estado alemán?
questions.explanation: Los colores evocan la bandera de Baviera; BMW se fundó en Múnich en 1916.

questions.question: ¿De qué marca de neumáticos es mascota Bibendum, el muñeco hecho de ruedas apiladas?
questions.explanation: Bibendum, el muñeco Michelin, representa a la marca francesa de neumáticos desde 1898.

quizzes.title: Brand Slogans Trivia: Which Company Said It?
quizzes.description: Eight questions on the most famous advertising slogans of all time, from 'Just Do It' to 'The Ultimate Driving Machine'.

questions.question: Which brand tells you to 'Just Do It'?
questions.explanation: Nike has used 'Just Do It' since 1988, making it one of the longest-running slogans in advertising.

questions.question: The slogan 'I'm Lovin' It' belongs to which fast food chain?
questions.explanation: Launched in 2003, 'I'm Lovin' It' was McDonald's first global advertising campaign.

questions.question: Which technology company told the world to 'Think Different'?
questions.explanation: Apple's 'Think Different' campaign ran from 1997 to 2002 and marked the company's comeback.

questions.question: 'Because You're Worth It' is the long-running slogan of which cosmetics brand?
questions.explanation: The L'Oréal slogan was written in 1971, originally as 'Because I'm Worth It'.

questions.question: Which candy promises to 'melt in your mouth, not in your hands'?
questions.explanation: M&M's have used the 'melts in your mouth, not in your hands' line since the 1950s.

questions.question: The slogan 'Have a break, have a...' ends with the name of which chocolate bar?
questions.explanation: 'Have a break, have a Kit Kat' has been the brand's slogan since 1958.

questions.question: Which carmaker calls itself 'The Ultimate Driving Machine'?
questions.explanation: BMW has used 'The Ultimate Driving Machine' in North America since the 1970s.

questions.question: 'Finger Lickin' Good' is the classic slogan of which fried chicken chain?
questions.explanation: KFC's 'Finger Lickin' Good' slogan dates back to the 1950s.

quizzes.title: Trivia de eslóganes de marcas: ¿qué empresa lo dice?
quizzes.description: Ocho preguntas sobre los eslóganes publicitarios más famosos de la historia, de 'Just Do It' a 'The Ultimate Driving Machine'.

questions.question: ¿Qué marca usa el eslogan 'Just Do It'?
questions.explanation: Nike usa 'Just Do It' desde 1988, uno de los eslóganes más longevos de la publicidad.

questions.question: El eslogan 'I'm Lovin' It' pertenece a qué cadena de comida rápida?
questions.explanation: Lanzado en 2003, 'I'm Lovin' It' fue la primera campaña publicitaria global de McDonald's.

questions.question: ¿Qué empresa de tecnología le dijo al mundo 'Think Different'?
questions.explanation: La campaña 'Think Different' de Apple estuvo vigente de 1997 a 2002.

questions.question: 'Because You're Worth It' ('Porque tú lo vales') es el eslogan de qué marca de cosméticos?
questions.explanation: El eslogan de L'Oréal se creó en 1971, originalmente como 'Because I'm Worth It'.

questions.question: ¿Qué dulce promete 'derretirse en tu boca, no en tus manos'?
questions.explanation: M&M's usa la frase 'se derrite en tu boca, no en tus manos' desde los años 50.

questions.question: El eslogan 'Have a break, have a...' termina con el nombre de qué chocolate?
questions.explanation: 'Have a break, have a Kit Kat' es el eslogan de la marca desde 1958.

questions.question: ¿Qué fabricante de autos se autodenomina 'The Ultimate Driving Machine'?
questions.explanation: BMW usa 'The Ultimate Driving Machine' en Norteamérica desde los años 70.

questions.question: 'Finger Lickin' Good' es el clásico eslogan de qué cadena de pollo frito?
questions.explanation: El eslogan 'Finger Lickin' Good' de KFC data de los años 50.

quizzes.title: Food Brands Trivia: The Companies Behind Your Favorite Products
quizzes.description: Eight questions on the origins and secrets of famous food and drink brands, from Coca-Cola to Chupa Chups.

questions.question: Which artist designed the daisy logo of the Spanish lollipop brand Chupa Chups?
questions.explanation: Salvador Dalí designed the Chupa Chups daisy logo in 1969 and placed it on top of the wrapper so it would always be visible.

questions.question: Coca-Cola was created in 1886 in which US city?
questions.explanation: Pharmacist John Pemberton invented Coca-Cola in Atlanta, Georgia, in 1886.

questions.question: Nutella is made by Ferrero, a company founded in which country?
questions.explanation: Ferrero is headquartered in Alba, in Italy's Piedmont region, where it was founded in 1946.

questions.question: The name of gummy brand Haribo combines founder Hans Riegel's name with which city?
questions.explanation: HA-RI-BO stands for Hans Riegel of Bonn, who founded the company in 1920.

questions.question: Heinz's famous slogan claims how many 'varieties'?
questions.explanation: Henry Heinz picked '57 varieties' in 1896, even though the company already sold more products.

questions.question: Kit Kat chocolate bars were first made in which country?
questions.explanation: Kit Kat was launched by Rowntree's of York, England, in 1935 as 'Rowntree's Chocolate Crisp'.

questions.question: Yogurt company Danone was founded in 1919 in which country?
questions.explanation: Isaac Carasso founded Danone in Barcelona and named it after his son Daniel's nickname.

questions.question: Which yeast-extract spread is a breakfast staple in Australia?
questions.explanation: Vegemite, launched in 1923, is the Australian counterpart of Britain's Marmite.

quizzes.title: Trivia de marcas de comida: las empresas detrás de tus productos favoritos
quizzes.description: Ocho preguntas sobre los orígenes y secretos de las marcas de comida y bebida más famosas, de Coca-Cola a Chupa Chups.

questions.question: ¿Qué artista diseñó el logo de margarita de la marca española Chupa Chups?
questions.explanation: Salvador Dalí diseñó el logo de margarita de Chupa Chups en 1969 y lo colocó en la parte superior del envoltorio.

questions.question: ¿En qué ciudad estadounidense se creó Coca-Cola en 1886?
questions.explanation: El farmacéutico John Pemberton inventó Coca-Cola en Atlanta, Georgia, en 1886.

questions.question: Nutella la fabrica Ferrero, una empresa fundada en qué país?
questions.explanation: Ferrero tiene su sede en Alba, en la región italiana del Piamonte, donde se fundó en 1946.

questions.question: El nombre de la marca de gomitas Haribo une el nombre del fundador Hans Riegel con qué ciudad?
questions.explanation: HA-RI-BO son las iniciales de Hans Riegel de Bonn, que fundó la empresa en 1920.

questions.question: ¿Cuántas 'variedades' promete el famoso eslogan de Heinz?
questions.explanation: Henry Heinz eligió el número 57 en 1896, aunque la empresa ya vendía más productos.

questions.question: ¿En qué país se fabricó por primera vez el chocolate Kit Kat?
questions.explanation: Kit Kat lo lanzó Rowntree's de York, Inglaterra, en 1935 como 'Rowntree's Chocolate Crisp'.

questions.question: ¿En qué país se fundó la empresa de yogures Danone en 1919?
questions.explanation: Isaac Carasso fundó Danone en Barcelona y la llamó así por el apodo de su hijo Daniel.

questions.question: ¿Qué pasta de extracto de levadura es un clásico del desayuno en Australia?
questions.explanation: Vegemite, lanzada en 1923, es la versión australiana de la británica Marmite.

quizzes.title: Tech Brands Trivia: How the Giants Got Started
quizzes.description: Eight questions on the surprising origins of tech giants, from a paper mill that became Nokia to Amazon's first product.

questions.question: Nintendo was founded in 1889 in Kyoto making which product?
questions.explanation: Nintendo spent its first decades making hanafuda playing cards; video games came almost a century later.

questions.question: Nokia, the mobile phone giant, began in 1865 as what kind of business?
questions.explanation: Nokia started as a pulp mill in Finland and later made rubber boots and cables before phones.

questions.question: Before electronics, Samsung began in 1938 as what kind of company?
questions.explanation: Samsung started as a small trading company in Korea selling dried fish, noodles and produce.

questions.question: Microsoft was founded in 1975 by which pair of friends?
questions.explanation: Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft in Albuquerque, New Mexico, in April 1975.

questions.question: Google was founded in 1998 by which Stanford PhD students?
questions.explanation: Page and Brin founded Google in 1998 and set up their first office in a garage in Menlo Park.

questions.question: Amazon, launched in 1994, originally sold only what?
questions.explanation: Amazon began as an online bookstore run from Jeff Bezos's garage in Bellevue, Washington.

questions.question: What is IBM's famous corporate nickname?
questions.explanation: IBM has been known as 'Big Blue' for decades, after its blue logo and mainframe computers.

questions.question: What was the first item sold on eBay in 1995?
questions.explanation: Founder Pierre Omidyar sold a broken laser pointer for $14.83; the buyer collected broken laser pointers.

quizzes.title: Trivia de marcas de tecnología: cómo empezaron los gigantes
quizzes.description: Ocho preguntas sobre los orígenes sorprendentes de los gigantes tecnológicos, de la fábrica de papel que se volvió Nokia al primer producto de Amazon.

questions.question: Nintendo se fundó en 1889 en Kioto fabricando qué producto?
questions.explanation: Nintendo pasó sus primeras décadas fabricando cartas hanafuda; los videojuegos llegaron casi un siglo después.

questions.question: Nokia, el gigante de los teléfonos móviles, empezó en 1865 como qué tipo de negocio?
questions.explanation: Nokia nació como una fábrica de pulpa de papel en Finlandia y luego hizo botas de goma y cables.

questions.question: Antes de la electrónica, Samsung empezó en 1938 como qué tipo de empresa?
questions.explanation: Samsung nació como una pequeña comercializadora en Corea que vendía pescado seco, fideos y verduras.

questions.question: ¿Qué pareja de amigos fundó Microsoft en 1975?
questions.explanation: Bill Gates y Paul Allen fundaron Microsoft en Albuquerque, Nuevo México, en abril de 1975.

questions.question: ¿Qué estudiantes de doctorado de Stanford fundaron Google en 1998?
questions.explanation: Page y Brin fundaron Google en 1998 y montaron su primera oficina en un garaje de Menlo Park.

questions.question: Amazon, lanzada en 1994, al principio solo vendía qué?
questions.explanation: Amazon empezó como una librería en línea operada desde el garaje de Jeff Bezos en Bellevue, Washington.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es el famoso apodo corporativo de IBM?
questions.explanation: IBM es conocida como 'Big Blue' desde hace décadas, por su logo azul y sus grandes computadoras.

questions.question: ¿Cuál fue el primer artículo vendido en eBay en 1995?
questions.explanation: El fundador Pierre Omidyar vendió un puntero láser roto por 14,83 dólares; el comprador los coleccionaba.

quizzes.title: Car Brand Origins Trivia: Where the Giants Come From
quizzes.description: Eight questions on where famous car brands were born and what they built before cars, from tractors to aircraft engines.

questions.question: The 911 sports car is built by a brand from which country?
questions.explanation: Porsche builds the 911 in Stuttgart, Germany, where the model has been made since 1964.

questions.question: Before building sports cars, Lamborghini made what?
questions.explanation: Ferruccio Lamborghini founded a tractor company in 1948; his sports car brand arrived in 1963.

questions.question: Volvo, famous for its safety focus, is a brand from which country?
questions.explanation: Volvo was founded in Gothenburg, Sweden, in 1927; its name means 'I roll' in Latin.

questions.question: Before making cars, Toyota's parent business produced what?
questions.explanation: Toyota grew out of Toyoda Automatic Loom Works, a maker of textile machinery.

questions.question: Hyundai, maker of the Tucson and the Elantra, is a brand from which country?
questions.explanation: Hyundai Motor Company was founded in Seoul, South Korea, in 1967.

questions.question: Fiat, maker of the 500, is headquartered in which Italian city?
questions.explanation: Fiat — Fabbrica Italiana Automobili Torino — has been based in Turin since 1899.

questions.question: BMW was founded in 1916 to build what?
questions.explanation: BMW began building aircraft engines in Munich; motorcycles and cars came in the 1920s.

questions.question: What does 'Volkswagen' literally mean in German?
questions.explanation: Volkswagen translates as 'people's car'; the company was founded in 1937.

quizzes.title: Trivia de orígenes de marcas de autos: de dónde vienen los gigantes
quizzes.description: Ocho preguntas sobre dónde nacieron las marcas de autos más famosas y qué fabricaban antes, de tractores a motores de avión.

questions.question: El deportivo 911 lo fabrica una marca de qué país?
questions.explanation: Porsche fabrica el 911 en Stuttgart, Alemania, donde el modelo se produce desde 1964.

questions.question: Antes de fabricar autos deportivos, Lamborghini hacía qué?
questions.explanation: Ferruccio Lamborghini fundó una empresa de tractores en 1948; su marca de deportivos llegó en 1963.

questions.question: Volvo, famosa por su enfoque en la seguridad, es una marca de qué país?
questions.explanation: Volvo se fundó en Gotemburgo, Suecia, en 1927; su nombre significa 'ruedo' en latín.

questions.question: Antes de fabricar autos, la empresa matriz de Toyota producía qué?
questions.explanation: Toyota nació de Toyoda Automatic Loom Works, un fabricante de maquinaria textil.

questions.question: Hyundai, fabricante del Tucson y del Elantra, es una marca de qué país?
questions.explanation: Hyundai Motor Company se fundó en Seúl, Corea del Sur, en 1967.

questions.question: Fiat, fabricante del 500, tiene su sede en qué ciudad italiana?
questions.explanation: Fiat —Fabbrica Italiana Automobili Torino— tiene su sede en Turín desde 1899.

questions.question: BMW se fundó en 1916 para fabricar qué?
questions.explanation: BMW empezó fabricando motores de avión en Múnich; las motos y los autos llegaron en los años 20.

questions.question: ¿Qué significa literalmente 'Volkswagen' en alemán?
questions.explanation: Volkswagen se traduce como 'auto del pueblo'; la empresa se fundó en 1937.
